title: Affine lifting of a free complex with its supplied unit coefficient
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, S=Spec R [def-weil-affine-spectrum], P a cochain complex [def-pc-derived-category] of O_S-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and n:Z→N. Supply identifications e_j:P^j≅O_S^{n(j)} [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Fix i and basis indices p in degree i and q in degree i+1 such that the (q,p) coefficient of e_{i+1}d^ie_i^{-1} is a unit of Γ(S,O_S). There exist a chain complex C of R-modules, m:Z→N, finite bases b_k indexed by Fin(m(k)), and indices p′ in degree -i and q′ in degree -i-1, such that m(-j)=n(j), the (q′,p′) coefficient of d_C at -i is a unit, and isomorphisms φ_j:tilde(C_{-j})≅P^j [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] with φ_k∘tilde(d_C(-j,-k))=d_P(j,k)∘φ_j for every adjacent j,k. This lifts the original complex; it does not assert cancellation or a homotopy equivalent complement.

source.place: Tags 01HV(1)-(2), 01I7: affine associated-sheaf comparison and its global-sections mapping property; read https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01HV and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I7; step 1 of lem-pc-affine-free-complex-unit-cancellation

proof.text: Take C_k = Γ(Spec R, P^(-k)), with R-action through (ΓSpecIso R).inv, and d_C(k,l) the global-sections map of d_P(-k,-l). Global sections sends zero morphisms to zero by evaluation, and functoriality sends d_P composed with d_P to zero. If l+1 is not k then -k+1 is not -l, so the cochain shape equation gives the chain shape equation. Set m(k)=n(-k). Compose the section isomorphism induced by e_(-k), freeSectionsEquiv, and coordinatewise (ΓSpecIso R).hom to obtain an R-linear equivalence C_k ≃ R^(ULift Fin m(k)). Basis.ofEquivFun and reindexing along Equiv.ulift give the required Fin bases. Double negation gives m(-j)=n(j).

For any f:M→N and supplied finite free identifications eM and eN, evaluate LinearMap.toMatrix in the bases obtained from the preceding section coordinates. Basis.ofEquivFun identifies a basis vector with the inverse image of Pi.single p 1. Since (ΓSpecIso R).inv preserves zero and one, its coordinatewise action fixes this standard vector. The proved freeSectionsEquiv_app formula says the conjugated map eM.inv ≫ f ≫ eN.hom acts by freeMatrix; multiplication by Pi.single p 1 selects column p. Thus the module coefficient at (q,p) equals (ΓSpecIso R).hom applied to that sheaf coefficient. Apply this calculation to d_P at the two negated degrees, cast the pivot indices along -(-i)=i and -(-i-1)=i+1, and use IsUnit.map. Reindexing the bases converts the same coefficient to the Fin-indexed matrix in the conclusion. All calculations hold over the zero ring and with empty finite index sets; the supplied pivots exclude an empty index set in either chosen degree.

Each P^j is in the essential image of tilde by tildeFinsupp composed with e_j.symm. Mathlib isIso_fromTildeΓ_iff therefore makes the canonical counit tilde(Γ(P^j))→P^j an isomorphism. Define φ_j by applying the global-sections and tilde functors to P.XIsoOfEq(-(-j)=j) and then composing with this counit isomorphism. Naturality of fromTildeΓNatTrans intertwines every differential. Functoriality and the XIsoOfEq_hom_comp_d and d_comp_XIsoOfEq_hom identities remove the two index transports, giving exactly the required differential equation.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_free_complex_module_lift (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (P : CochainComplex (Spec R).Modules ℤ) (n : ℤ → ℕ) (e : ∀ j : ℤ, P.X j ≅ SheafOfModules.free (R := (Spec R).ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin (n j)))) (i : ℤ) (p : ULift.{u} (Fin (n i))) (q : ULift.{u} (Fin (n (i + 1)))) (hunit : IsUnit (freeMatrix ((e i).inv ≫ P.d i (i + 1) ≫ (e (i + 1)).hom) q p)) : ∃ (C : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (m : ℤ → ℕ) (b : ∀ k : ℤ, Module.Basis (Fin (m k)) R (C.X k)) (p' : Fin (m (-i))) (q' : Fin (m (-i - 1))), (∀ j : ℤ, m (-j) = n j) ∧ IsUnit (LinearMap.toMatrix (b (-i)) (b (-i - 1)) (C.d (-i) (-i - 1)).hom q' p') ∧ ∃ φ : ∀ j : ℤ, tilde (C.X (-j)) ≅ P.X j, ∀ j k : ℤ, (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel j k → (φ j).hom ≫ P.d j k = tilde.map (C.d (-j) (-k)) ≫ (φ k).hom
